summary: Lolo National Forest L-4 tower near St. Regis, Montana, built 1937 and destroyed 1973; listed as gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1973; the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Montana list marks it as gone

events.note: Firelookout.com lists it as an L-4 tower built in 1937
Firelookout.com says 'Destroyed 1973'; the page gives no cause

evidence.supports: the lookout is in the Lolo National Forest
about 11 miles northwest of St. Regis
listed as a tower with status Gone

notes_for_editor: Two pages only. Firelookout.com gives the build year, destruction year, location and elevation in a few lines; the FFLA Montana list gives status only. The story is about 100 words, under the 120-word floor, because nothing else found describes this site. Not the same as Mineral Peak (Lolo NF, standing, NHLR; described in the NRHP multiple-property form), and not the Idaho lookout called Mineral Ridge on willhiteweb.com; neither was used. Cause of the 1973 destruction is not given by any source found. Two WebSearch calls used.
